analysis.title: Cell towers have entered a new era of opportunity
key_insights: Tower REITs gained 18.6% in October through the 23rd, after declining 10.6% year to date through September 30. Year-to-date returns are back in positive territory.

Reports that SpaceX is considering a sizable terrestrial network drove a one-day 5.2% climb in tower REITs on October 23. Cohen & Steers argues satellite connectivity could add tower demand rather than displace it.
Cohen & Steers forecasts tower cash flow growth approaching 5% in 2027 and more than 6% in 2028 as prior headwinds fade.

The 2021-2025 share price weakness came from Sprint network consolidation, DISH lease cancellations, slower carrier investment after the initial 5G buildout, asset sales and higher refinancing costs. The firm says the Sprint and DISH cancellations were one-time events now substantially reflected in results.
No remaining tenant outside the three national carriers represents more than 1% of U.S. tower revenue, which lowers the risk of another comparable cancellation cycle.

A sizable new terrestrial network build could add approximately 100-200 basis points to current net organic revenue growth over a multi-year deployment, without requiring more activity from the three incumbent carriers. Much of that revenue would use infrastructure already in place, so the effect on cash flow could be outsized.

Towers trade at a 4.1x price-to-cash-flow discount to the broader REIT market, versus a 6.6x premium in 2020. Cohen & Steers says cash flow growth could narrow the gap and produce returns from both earnings growth and re-rating.

Towers deliver capacity in dense, high-usage areas, and satellites extend coverage to remote areas where terrestrial buildout is uneconomic. The firm treats the two as complementary rather than competing.
The recovery case does not depend on SpaceX or on faster spending by the national carriers. Either would be incremental upside to the existing outlook.

sector_views.rationale: Headwinds are fading, cash flow growth is forecast to recover to about 5% in 2027 and above 6% in 2028, and valuations sit at a 4.1x price-to-cash-flow discount to REITs.

earnings_insights: Cohen & Steers forecasts tower cash flow growth approaching 5% in 2027 and more than 6% in 2028 (firm estimate, not reported results).
risk_factors: The size and scope of any SpaceX terrestrial deployment remain uncertain.
Carrier investment could stay slow, though the firm's recovery case does not rely on a pickup.
Higher interest rates raised refinancing costs and compressed valuations over 2021-2025.
